thread:
maria_cs: FYI onboarding for HelioHealth hit repeated latency breaches this morning. Need to align on credits and a short customer note. TL;DR: p99 spiked to ~2.6s for 10m starting 08:12 PST.

oncall-bot: Alert: latency_spike detected for customer=heliohealth, route=gen-long, window=600s, p99=2.62s — https://logs.internal/alerts/2148884321

dylan_ops: Can you paste the metric snippet and which model/route they were hitting? Need to know if this was a routing failure or overload.

maria_cs: Route = gen-long, model pinned = rdx-7b-q3 (customer dedicated pool). Saw burst during onboarding batch onboarding-job-772. I pulled p50/p90/p99: 0.35s / 0.9s / 2.62s.

olivia_eng: Looking. Initial guess: KV cache warm + a few very long contexts from their dataset. I see sustained seq_len long tails in the trace. Also a couple of worker restarts around 08:14 — stack shows oom-restart on gpu-2.

kevin_prod: If worker restarts occurred, we should check autoscale/burst config for that dedicated pool. Also consider temporary fallback to rdx-7b-quant which recovers faster under cache churn.

maria_cs: Important for the customer convo: they expect a credit if SLO was missed during onboarding ramp. What's our calc method here? Do we pro-rate onboarding time?

sam_account_mgr: Typically we compute outage window where p99>1.5s (their latency SLO) and pro-rate against monthly committed uptime. For a short onboarding window we split applied credit bucket: min 1% credit up to 10% depending on recurrence. But let's confirm legal approved formula.

olivia_eng: From infra side, this looks like a transient degradation (worker oom -> restart). We can contain: 1) rollback any recent model kernel changes on that pool (none flagged), 2) increase burst capacity by +1 GPU for the pool for next 24h, 3) enable fallback route to quant variant. I'll open a deploy ticket.

maria_cs: Draft customer note suggestion: "We observed transient latency degradation during your onboarding batch. Root cause: worker memory pressure leading to restarts; we applied a fallback route and increased burst capacity. No data loss. As a goodwill gesture we propose a 2% credit for this onboarding window; we can discuss if you prefer a different remediation." Thoughts?

kevin_prod: 2% seems reasonable for a single ~10m spike. Ops should confirm exact downwindow minutes — we need the precise minutes to compute prorated credit. If repeated within 30 days escalate to 5%.

dylan_ops: I can compute exact downwindow from logs. Quick snippet I'll run: 
```
# query p99 by minute
query = "service:inference p99{route:gen-long} by minute where customer=heliohealth and ts in [2148880321..2148884321]"
```
I'll post numbers in 10m.

oncall-bot: Incident ticket INC-214888-HELI created and assigned to olivia_eng, priority=P2.

olivia_eng: Opening a quick runbook: will 1) drain new sessions from gpu-2 2) scale +1 GPU 3) enable fallback to rdx-7b-quant for 2 hours 4) monitor p99 for next 6 hours.

maria_cs: Timeline and owners please for the email and credit calc. We need to get back to the customer before EOD.

sam_account_mgr: I'll draft the customer-facing note in #templates and circulate. dylan_ops please post the exact downwindow minutes + minute-by-minute p99 so I can compute the credit using the template.

dylan_ops: Posted downwindow: 08:12:00 - 08:22:00 (10 minutes) with p99s: [2.6,2.5,2.3,1.8,1.4,1.2,0.9,0.6,0.5,0.45] — so effective breach until 08:16:00 (4 minutes >1.5s). Sending the raw CSV in DM.

sam_account_mgr: Using template calc: (4 minutes / total minutes in billing period)*commit_percent => 2% credit rounded to nearest 0.5%. I'll send the customer note and cc legal.

maria_cs: Great. Olivia, once escalations are applied ping here so I can update HelioHealth. Also capture a short postmortem blurb for onboarding playbook.

olivia_eng: Will do. Scaling and fallback applied at 08:30 and p99 returned to baseline by 09:00. Adding runbook steps to onboarding checklist.

maria_cs: Thanks all. I'll send the note after legal quick check. :white_check_mark:
